SMTO-GWT-0019 — The request to the Gateway was too large

GUID: e0a13544-f146-4038-a86e-72c9d986c9de
Slug: gateway-request-too-large
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO tried to send more data to the computer in one request than the Gateway accepts, so the Gateway refused it before doing anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task included a big file or a lot of pasted text, ask for the work in smaller parts. Each part then fits within what the Gateway accepts in one request.
  2. For large files, ask SMTO to copy the file to that computer instead of putting its contents into a command. Copying a file sends it in pieces, which avoids the size limit.
  3. Run the task again with the smaller request. The Gateway refused the large request before doing anything, so nothing needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • The task finishes on that computer without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete saved results or files to make the request fit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's authentication middleware read more request body bytes than the applicable limit (pairing, binary transfer frame or 64 MiB general request) and rejected it before dispatch.

What this means

  • The authentication middleware read more body bytes than the applicable pairing, binary-transfer or general request limit before dispatch. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication middleware read more body bytes than the applicable pairing, binary-transfer or general request limit before dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the request route and its body limit; compare the serialized payload size rather than just the source file size.

How to fix it

  • ControllerAuthMiddleware limits bodies to 16 KiB for pairing (PAIR_BODY), one transfer_wire frame for binary transfer, and 64 MiB (MAX_BODY) otherwise. Reduce the request payload (for example split large content) or move large data with the Gateway's file transfer support instead of embedding it in a command.
  • Reduce the payload or use the supported file transfer capability.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended request fits the route's bound and passes authenticated admission.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
